svg.title: Conflict-based search on the same example
svg.desc: CBS plans each AGV alone, finds the conflict at vertex 3, branches on which AGV must avoid it, and expands the cheaper branch. Here it finds a plan with a lower total time than prioritized planning.
svg.metadata: ["Root of the constraint tree: plan each AGV alone, ignoring the other. Total cost (sum of arrival times) 6 + 4 = 10, but both use vertex 3 between 2 s and 4 s: a conflict.", "Branch 1: forbid AGV-2 from vertex 3 while AGV-1 is there. Only AGV-2 is replanned (SIPP): it waits at 6 and arrives at 10 s. Cost 16.", "Branch 2: forbid AGV-1 from vertex 3 while AGV-2 is there. AGV-1 waits at 2 and arrives at 8 s; AGV-2 goes straight. Cost 12.", "CBS always expands the cheapest open node. Branch 2 has the lower cost and no conflict, so it is the solution; with sum-of-costs as the objective it is optimal.", "Same input, different answer: prioritized planning committed to e1 first and paid 16. CBS needs the same pieces, a graph, start and goal per agent, a conflict test and a single-agent planner, but searches over who yields."]

g.text: CBS (Sharon et al. 2015) keeps a tree of constraint sets. Each node replans only the constrained agent with a single-agent search, checks for the first conflict and, if there is one,

g.text: branches into two children, one per agent that could give way.
